surface_forms: la dame à coiffure blanche de Marie-Antoinette
la dame coiffée à la Marie-Antoinette

appraisal_events.evidence: abaissa légèrement la tête avec une majesté glaciale et la tournant d'un autre côté ne s'occupa pas plus de moi que si je n'eusse pas existé.
appraisal_events.explanation: Upon being introduced, Alix pointedly ignores the narrator, performing icy indifference to signal that she has connections to spare and no interest in him.

appraisal_events.evidence: elle me glissa à l'oreille de venir le vendredi suivant dans sa loge, avec une des trois dont le nom éclatant... me fit un prodigieux effet.
appraisal_events.explanation: Moments later, in private, Alix draws the narrator into her exclusive theatre box alongside a woman of a resounding name, a mark of favor that visibly dazzles him -- a separate, later moment from the public snub.

appraisal_events.evidence: L'étonnement de Bloch allait grandissant. « Mésalliée, la Maison de France ? Comment ça ? — Mais en s'alliant aux Médicis », répondit Mme de Villeparisis du ton le plus naturel.
appraisal_events.explanation: Bloch's escalating bewilderment at elementary aristocratic genealogy is played for comic exposure, contrasting with Mme de Villeparisis's effortlessly natural mastery of the same lore.

appraisal_events.evidence: vous vous rappelez que quand je vous ai amené Liszt il vous a dit que c'était celui-là qui était la copie. — Je m'inclinerai devant une opinion de Liszt en musique, mais pas en peinture !... Mais ce n'est pas vous qui me l'avez amené. J'avais dîné vingt fois avec lui chez la princesse de Sayn-Wittgenstein.
appraisal_events.explanation: Alix challenges the authenticity of Mme de Villeparisis's prized portrait by invoking Liszt's supposed verdict and her own claim to have introduced him; Mme de Villeparisis flatly denies both the verdict's relevance and the introduction, asserting a far closer, long-standing acquaintance with Liszt of her own.

status_effects.explanation: He is publicly treated as if he did not exist, held outside Alix's notice at the moment of introduction.
In a separate, private moment, he is admitted across a different boundary -- invited into Alix's own theatre box alongside a grandly named guest, a clear mark of favor he finds dazzling.
His repeated, growing astonishment at basic aristocratic genealogy plays as naive in contrast to the ease with which the point is made to him.
Her natural, unhesitating command of aristocratic lore quietly outclasses Bloch's confusion in the same exchange.
In a distinct, later exchange, she firmly wins the dispute over the portrait's authenticity and her own claim to intimacy with Liszt, flatly rebutting Alix's challenge.
Her claim about Liszt's verdict and her own role in introducing him is flatly denied and left looking overstated or false.

ambiguities: Alix's private invitation to her loge (E2) could be read either as genuine favor or as a further move in the same calculated social gamesmanship evident in her public snub, but the passage foregrounds the narrator's dazzled reaction, so the positive local movement is preserved.
